prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” lawyer for everyone — the right personal-injury attorney for a car wreck depends on the crash facts, how serious the injuries are, whether liability is disputed, and your preferences (trial lawyer vs. settlement-focused, communication style, fee terms, etc.). I can help you find a good match. First, important quick points:

- Statute of limitations: In Texas you generally have 2 years from the date of the wreck to file a personal-injury suit, so act quickly.
- Look for lawyers who focus on motor-vehicle collisions and personal injury (not general practice).
- Board certification in Personal Injury Trial Law (Texas Board of Legal Specialization) and a record of jury verdicts/trial experience are big pluses if your case may go to trial.
- Most reputable personal-injury lawyers handle car-wreck cases on contingency (no fee unless you recover money).

How to find the best lawyer for your case
1. Check reputable sources:
   - Texas Board of Legal Specialization (for board-certified trial lawyers)
   - Houston Trial Lawyers Association and Houston Bar Association member directories
   - Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell (peer reviews), and Google/Yelp reviews
2. Narrow to attorneys who:
   - Regularly handle car-accident and bodily-injury claims
   - Have recent settlements/verdicts for similar injuries
   - Will commit to clear communication and explain fees/expenses in writing
3. Interview 3–4 lawyers (most offer free consultations). Ask:
   - How many car-wreck cases do you handle each year?
   - Do you handle these in-house or refer parts to others?
   - Have you tried similar cases to verdict? Examples of outcomes?
   - Who will handle day-to-day communication (you or staff)?
   - What is your contingency fee and who pays case expenses?
   - Do you think my case will settle or need trial?
   - What is your estimate of case value and timeline, and why?
4. Red flags:
   - Guarantees of a specific dollar amount
   - High-pressure tactics to sign immediately
   - No written fee/retainer agreement or unclear expense policy

If you want, tell me your ZIP code or the neighborhood where the crash happened and a one-line summary of injuries/complexity (e.g., “minor injuries, clear liability” vs “catastrophic injuries, disputed fault”), and I’ll suggest how to find 3–5 local attorneys to call and provide a short script and checklist for your consultations.
